Yamada's theorem plus the canonical Seifert surface gives c>=2g+b-1, and that lower bound equals the displayed braid length exactly. The same source identifies every complement in the stated hyperbolic range as a nontrivial filling of one fixed hyperbolic manifold M=S^3\L14n61770; strict hyperbolic Dehn-filling volume decrease gives Vol(K)<Vol(M).

value.rationale: Crossing number, braid/bridge index and hyperbolic volume are basic but substantially different knot-complexity measures. For a newly introduced asymmetric L-space family, the theorem computes crossing number exactly and shows that braid/bridge index and quadratic crossing complexity can diverge while volume stays uniformly bounded. The explicit density bound gives a reusable quantitative separation rather than a routine single-parameter restatement.
